raw_response:
I have farmed a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked on my land before and then I adjust a little. On 5 mu, I will still put most of my land into cotton, because that is my main crop and it brings the bigger return if the stand is good. I have well water, so I am not as scared of dry spells as people who depend only on rain. For cotton, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I have seen the newer kinds hold bolls better and make picking more worthwhile. I will put enough fertilizer to keep the plants growing steady: more nitrogen for stems and bolls, some phosphate under the base fertilizer so roots start strong, and potash too because cotton eats fertilizer and I do not want it to drop bolls halfway. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. For mungbean, I will keep a smaller area. That crop does not need as much fertilizer, and if I push too much nitrogen it grows too much vine and not enough pods. I will use it on the lighter part of the land and manage it simpler than cotton. Labor in my house is only two people, so I cannot spread myself too thin with too much delicate work. I will plough before planting because old habits still matter, and on my ground ploughing lets water and fertilizer go in better than leaving the soil hard. This year I will keep cotton as the money crop and mungbean as the lighter, lower-cost crop, balancing fertilizer money, pesticide money, and the labor we can actually handle.
